finding.claim: Broken authorization on the ban endpoint. The admin check is wrapped in try/except Exception, which swallows the 403 raised by abort(). Any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users. The unban endpoint lacks the try/except, so the two endpoints are inconsistent.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user (g.user with is_admin falsy) sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid), the privileged ban operation, at admin.py:20.

trace.note: The route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST. uid is attacker-chosen.
A non-admin makes require_admin call abort(403), which raises werkzeug HTTPException (a subclass of Exception).
The handler only logs a warning (which also logs the user name). It does not re-raise or return.
The handler returns ok=True, so the non-admin's ban succeeds.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin raises 403 correctly, but its exception is swallowed by the caller. No other decorator, before_request hook or middleware exists in the file. The unban route at admin.py:26 calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is correctly protected. The authentication that populates g.user is not in this codebase, so it was assumed to run outside this file.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but ban() wraps it in try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19), which swallows the error. No decorator, before_request hook or other guard exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20, the HTTPException raised by abort(403) at line 11 is caught by `except Exception`, which only logs, so do_ban(uid) runs and returns ok=True for any non-admin who reaches the route. The unban route at line 26 has no try/except, so it is protected. One small imprecision: the abort is on line 11, and the trace cites line 10, which is the condition.
